Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The method ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2) fails when handling arrays of mixed types that share a common supertype, such as Integer[] and Long[], both of which can be assigned to Number[]. The method implementation first checks for null arrays and clones the non-null array if one of the inputs is null; otherwise, it proceeds to concatenate the two arrays.

In the implementation, the component type of the first array is extracted with array1.getClass().getComponentType(). Then, using Java reflection, a new array is created with the component type of the first array and a length equal to the sum of the lengths of the two input arrays. The method uses System.arraycopy to copy the contents of the first and second arrays into the new array.

The problem arises on the line where array2 is copied into the joinedArray. The joinedArray's component type is fixed as the component type of array1 (e.g., Integer), but array2 might have a different component type (e.g., Long). At runtime, this leads to an ArrayStoreException because the Long element cannot be stored in an Integer array.

The test case tries to cover this problem:
- When adding Number[] arrays (Integer[] and Long[] stored as Number[]) it works fine.
- When the actual element types are incompatible, for example adding Integer[] and Long[], the code throws ArrayStoreException rather than a clearer IllegalArgumentException.

The current bug report points out the confusing nature of ArrayStoreException in this scenario, evolving from the raw System.arraycopy call. A better design would detect type incompatibility earlier and throw a more informative exception.

Hence, the root cause is that the addAll method blindly uses the component type of the first input array to create the result array without verifying that the second array elements can fit in that type, leading to a potentially opaque ArrayStoreException.

Potential fix: Before array copying, validate type compatibility between the arrays and throw a clear IllegalArgumentException if incompatible.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
